problem: A surface $S$ is defined by $z=f(x,y).$ The curve $C$ is the intersection of $S$ with the plane $x=2.$ Given that the point $P$ with $y$-coordinate $1$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{y}=3{x}^{2}y-6x{y}^{2}$, find the slope of the tangent to $C$ at $P.$

feedback.problem: A surface $S$ is defined by $z=f(x,y).$ The curve $C$ is the intersection of $S$ with the plane $y=3.$ Given that the point $P(2,3,9)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{x}=6x-y$, find the slope of the tangent to $C$ at $P.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $y=3.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point $P(2,3,9)$ will be given by the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(2,3).$

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ at $(2,3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(2,3) & =6(2)-(3)=9\end{aligned}
$$
